pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Profiling Qwen-Image 2.1 (1024x1024, 40 steps, bf16, `--attention-backend torch_sdpa`) on one SM120 GPU shows each transformer block spending ~10.8 ms per step: 81% GEMM, 14% attention and ~5% everything else. That last slice was not bandwidth-limited work but data movement and launches around attention:

- two Triton kernels for Q/K RMSNorm + complex RoPE (`_qknorm_complex_rope_onepass_kernel`, 38 us; `_qknorm_complex_rope_kv_kernel`, 119 us), the second of which re-copies the full V projection (64 MiB per block-step) just to place it behind the text prefix;
- three separate Q/K/V GEMMs (N=4096 each) with their own tile tails;
- a single-element `torch.cat` on the attention output that degrades to a 33.5 MB device copy.

All three are removed here without changing a single output bit: every new path is default-on and verifies its first call against the eager chain through `BitExactFusionGate`, falling back permanently on a mismatch (the existing Qwen-Image 2.1 convention).

## Modifications

One commit per optimization:

1. `bef0002567` **Skip the single-element `torch.cat`** on the attention output (pure aliasing; the multi-segment prefix path keeps the cat).
2. `50f14915a4` **`qknorm_complex_rope` JIT CUDA kernel** (`kernels/jit/csrc/diffusion/qknorm_complex_rope.cuh`, wrapper `ops/diffusion/rope/qknorm_complex_rope_jit.py`). One warp per 128-wide row; Q and K RMSNorm (`RMSNorm(cast_x_before_out_mul=True)`: aten's 128-wide fp32 reduction order and double bf16 rounding), the complex64 RoPE with the same FMA orientation as the Triton path (`_fuse_real_sin` probe), and the prefix K/V copies in a single launch. `run` (out of place, used by `apply_qk_norm_rope`) and `run_pack` (Q in place, K normalized in place behind the prefix rows, optional V copy) variants; registered as custom ops with fake impls; CUDA-graph safe.
3. `622f00a077` **K/V projections written straight into the packed KV buffers**: `torch.mm(x, W.t(), out=buffer[P:])` for K and V so V is never copied and the kernel normalizes K in place (`kCopyV=False`). Gated by a first-sight `torch.equal` against the module forward.
4. `30819672a1` **One packed Q/K/V GEMM**: `to_q/to_k/to_v` weights are re-pointed at slices of one `[3C, C]` storage in `post_load_weights` (the per-layer `weight` parameters stay views, so checkpoint loading, weight updates and LoRA base weights are unaffected); one N=12288 GEMM writes into a `[1, P+S, 3C]` buffer and Q/K/V are column views (token stride 3C) consumed by the pack kernel and SDPA. Gated by a first-sight compare with the three separate GEMMs.
5. `3a2dd56e1f` gate protocol tests, kernel README row, fast-paths inventory entry, pre-commit formatting (a marker benchmark added here was dropped again later in the series).

Fallbacks keep the previous Triton chain: batch > 1, sequence parallel > 1, LoRA-wrapped or quantized projections, head_dim != 128, ROCm, `torch.compile`, and any first-sight mismatch. Nothing is verified while a CUDA graph is being captured.

Per block-step the op sequence goes from 7 GEMM + 1 attention + 8 small kernels + 1 memcpy to 5 GEMM + 1 attention + 6 small kernels.

## Accuracy Tests

Everything in this PR is bit-exact by construction and verified at three levels:

- Kernel: `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_qknorm_complex_rope.py` (20 cases; `torch.equal` against `RMSNorm(cast_x_before_out_mul=True, force_native=True)` + eager complex RoPE; shapes (1,4096,32,128), (1,18,32,128), (2,17,4,128), (1,1,1,128); in-place and copy pack variants; token-strided views of a packed QKV buffer; CUDA graph replay).
- Wiring: `test_model_fast_paths.py::test_qwen21_cuda_qk_rope_*` (first-sight verify, mismatch -> permanent eager fallback, no verification during capture) and `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image21_cuda.py` (head_dim-128 model: prefill + cached steps in t2i and edit mode with `atol=0`, prefix cache stays exact-size storage, breakable-CUDA-graph capture/replay `atol=0`, packed weights share storage and survive in-place updates, pack mismatch restores the reference).
- End to end: the same-seed 1024x1024 PNG (seed 42, `generator_device=cpu`) has the same sha256 as `main` in every launch of this series (`2781b27ac4b17cb1...`, 12 launches on two GPUs).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware: one cc 12.0 (SM120) GPU, 73 GB, 350 W power cap, clocks not locked (the GPU sits at the cap during the whole run); torch 2.13.0+cu132, cuDNN 9.20. Workload: `sglang serve --performance-mode speed --attention-backend torch_sdpa`, 1024x1024, 40 steps, guidance 1.0, bf16, eager. Each e2e number is one server launch with 1 warmup + 3 measured requests; stage times come from `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1`.

Kernel level (`marker.do_bench` on the production shapes, median us):

| site | eager | Triton (main) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q RMSNorm + RoPE, (1, 4096, 32, 128) | 548.9 | 65.5 | 65.5 (same bytes; kept for the pack variant) |
| Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE + KV packing, S=4096, P=18 | 1133.6 | 190.5 (two kernels, copies V) | 124.9 (K in place, V never copied) |
| Q/K/V projection, M=4096, K=4096 | - | 3 x N=4096: 1786 | 1 x N=12288: 1707 |

End to end (denoising stage, 32 blocks x 40 steps; e2e HTTP latency of the DiT-only tree on the same GPU as its baseline):

| tree | denoising 40 steps (ms) | per block-step (us) | e2e HTTP (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 13 715 | 342.9 x 1 / 32 | 13.890 |
| this PR | 13 533 (-1.3%) | -142 per block-step | 13.721 (-1.2%) |

The -142 us per block-step decomposes (nsys, same GPU) into -70 us from the packed GEMM (six 64x256 GEMM launches at 6717 us -> four at 6647 us), -55 us from the single norm-RoPE launch (104 us vs 38 + 119 us) and -15 us from the removed memcpy. Whole-image kernel launches drop from 24 699 to about 20 800. The GPU stays at its power cap; the fused tree runs ~18 MHz lower at the same 347 W, so the gain under locked clocks would be slightly larger. Run-to-run spread of the e2e latency is 0.3-1.0%; the -1.3% was reproduced in three interleaved rounds.

Smoke of this exact branch (rebased on `main` @ `3ed56a341b`, one launch each on a second GPU of the same type, stage-profiling cohort): `main` 13.894 s / denoising 13 585 ms; this PR 13.735 s / denoising 13 427 ms (-158 ms), PNG sha256 identical.

Not done here (measured and rejected): fusing the residual gate add with the following LayerNorm (the two-kernel chain is L2-resident and the fused kernel was slower, 114.5 vs 105.9 us), packing the gate/up GEMMs into one N=24576 GEMM (462 us/block-step slower on this GPU), and rewriting `_silu_mul_kernel` in CUDA (it already runs at 1.28 TB/s of a 1.34 TB/s roofline).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
